name: MIPLIB 2017 open instance rocII-10-11
description: Find a feasible solution of the MIPLIB 2017 instance rocII-10-11 with as low an objective value as possible (a maximisation model is negated, so that lower is better for every instance). A solution is feasible when every variable bound, every row bound and the integrality of every integer variable hold within an absolute tolerance of 1e-6 on the values as they are returned; integer variables are not rounded first.
contract: solve(model) -> numpy array of num_cols values, one per column. model has name, mps_path (the uncompressed MPS file), num_cols, num_rows, A (scipy CSR matrix of the rows), col_cost, col_lower, col_upper, row_lower, row_upper, integrality (bool array), offset, maximise and indicators (a list of (row, column, value): such a row has to hold only when that column equals the value; empty for most instances). Score: col_cost @ x + offset in minimisation form (negated when maximise is true), minimized; an infeasible vector is invalid.
notes: Listed objective -11.7943245021343 (in the model's own sense).
Optimal control of a bounded-confidence opinion dynamics system (steering the opinions of a group of agents), submitted by Joerg Rambau and imported from the MIPLIB 2010 submissions.
The objective listed on the open-instances page may have been improved since 2026-11-11 (the list did not change between 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-11).
Candidates may call HiGHS through highspy; a stronger solver is a method, not a discovery by the workflow.
The starting program finds no feasible solution of this instance (HiGHS with a 30 s limit, run of 2026-11-11), so a search starts from an invalid candidate.

science_relevance.reason: The paper has optimal control of agents in a bounded-confidence opinion dynamics as its main objective, which is the problem of the MIPLIB submission.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Choose controls for a strategic agent that steers the opinions of the other agents in a deterministic bounded-confidence (Hegselmann-Krause type) opinion dynamics over a finite horizon, as a mixed-integer program (instance rocII-10-11).
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Opinion dynamics models how opinions form in societies; optimal control of them asks how a campaign can best influence a group, and the resulting mixed-integer programs are hard for general solvers.
